pending_commit.commit_message: kerberos: Add TgtRenewalScheduler class TgtRenewalScheduler is responsible for scheduling automatic Kerberos ticket-granting-ticket (TGT) renewals. Usually, TGTs are valid for 8-10 hours and can be renewed periodically for a week or 2, which refreshes the validity lifetime each time until the renewal lifetime limit is hit. TgtRenewalScheduler schedules renewal tasks. If the ticket lifetime is 10 hours, it schedules automatic renewals after 6h0m, 8h24m, 9h21m, 9h44m, 9h53m and 9h 57m. If all these attempts failed, it will send a notification that the ticket is about to expire. If the ticket was already expired, e.g. after waking up from a suspended state, it sends out a notification that the ticket has already expired. The class is not used yet. This is done in a follow-up CL. BUG=chromium:952242 TEST=Unit test Change-Id: Ice4ceac8432b6055098e2773ac4baa11632e3bcf Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1680417 Tested-by: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org>

kerberos: Automatically renew Kerberos tickets Uses a TgtRenewalScheduler for each Kerberos account to automatically renew Kerberos tickets. If renewal fails, the code attempts to acquire a fresh ticket if the login password or a previously remembered password are available. If that fails as well, it emits a KerberosTicketExpiring notification 3 minutes before a ticket expires, so Chrome can pop up a notification. BUG=chromium:952242 TEST=Enable KerberosEnabled policy, go to chrome:settings/kerberosAccounts, add an account (e.g. using a chromeadm-lab.com account), add ticket_lifetime=10m to the configuration. Unplug network. Wait 7 minutes. You should eventually see a notification to refresh the ticket. With network plugged in, the ticket should renew and there should be not notification. Change-Id: I4a519082ffff1d518b639c612d4045607962b372 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1681758 Tested-by: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Roman Sorokin [CET] <rsorokin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org>

kerberos: Add setuid policy Adds a policy that allows kerberosd to only switch to kerberosd-exec and kerberosd-exec to switch to nowhere. The kerberos daemon runs as kerberosd and will switch to kerberosd-exec to run untrusted code in a future CL. The policy prevents the untrusted code to gain access to sensitive data like passwords. See also chromium:1683954. BUG=chromium:973391 TEST=Compiles, verified that policy gets installed. kukui: unset wait_ext_is_fake and shorten reset_recovery wait_ext_is_fake was mistakenly set to yes in Kukui's initial commit. This causes a lot of FAFT failures. Unset it to use the default value (no). Also, reset_recovery should be set to the time period required from cold_reset release to EC UART ready. This delay shouldn't be too long or AP might boot too far and modify the recovery reason. After some measurements, 0.6s should be good. device: Read boot time VPD values from raw blob For security concern the kernel VPD driver (which exports /sys/firmware/vpd) does not allow key names with dot, but that is currently used by factory for manufacturing stage only. The VPD utility (/usr/sbin/vpd) supports names with dot, but reading firmware image from SPI is pretty slow on many systems, so we do want to read from the VPD cache from kernel driver. Since chromium:1686805, `vpd` now supports a '--raw' option that can decode from /sys/firmware/vpd/{ro,rw}_raw and we may use that in boot time for fetching VPD quickly.
